summary: The new _set_timeout helper has its condition inverted, so it never applies the client timeout to requests lacking one and would instead overwrite explicit timeouts.

findings.explanation: `if "timeout" in request.extensions` is inverted. For a bare httpx.Request (the case this PR targets) no timeout key exists, so nothing is set and the client timeout is still ignored; for requests built via build_request (which already carry a timeout) it replaces the per-request timeout with the client default.

`isinstance(self.timeout, UseClientDefault)` is the wrong check: self.timeout is a Timeout (never UseClientDefault), so it always goes to Timeout(self.timeout). The intent is to use self.timeout directly when it is already a Timeout.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `self.timeout if isinstance(self.timeout, Timeout) else Timeout(self.timeout)`.

findings.explanation: Only an async test is added; the sync Client.send path also changed and is untested. With a 1e-6 timeout the async test would also pass for the wrong reasons if any timeout were applied.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sync test and a test that an explicit per-request timeout is preserved.
